nodes.summary: Chow–Liu's approximation `P_τ` as a probability mass function.
nodes.title: Chow–Liu approximation as a probability mass function

nodes.summary: `P ≪ P_τ`: the approximation is positive wherever `p` is.
nodes.title: Joint law is absolutely continuous w.r.t. its Chow–Liu approximation

nodes.summary: Chow–Liu's product approximation `P_τ(x) = ∏_i P(x_i | x_{j(i)})` of a joint law `p`, with the marginal `P(x_i)` for a parentless `i`. The conditional `P(x_i | x_j)` is `P(x_i, x_j) / P(x_j)`; where `P(x_j) = 0` the quotient is `0`, and such `x` have `P(x) = 0`.
nodes.title: Chow–Liu product approximation of a joint law

nodes.summary: A dependence forest on the variables `ι` (Chow–Liu 1968): each variable has at most one parent, and `rank` strictly increases from parent to child, so the parent relation has no cycles.
nodes.title: Dependence forest

nodes.summary: `divergence` is Mathlib's Kullback–Leibler divergence `klDiv` of `P` relative to `P_τ`, converted to bits; the finite alphabet carries the discrete σ-algebra.
nodes.title: Chow–Liu divergence as a Kullback–Leibler divergence

nodes.summary: Among dependence forests, a smaller divergence is the same as a larger mutual-information weight, so minimizing `D(P ‖ P_τ)` over dependence trees is maximizing the total mutual information `∑_i I(X_i; X_{j(i)})` of their edges.
nodes.title: Chow–Liu optimality

nodes.summary: The divergence of `P` from Chow–Liu's approximation is nonnegative, so `∑_i I(X_i; X_{j(i)}) ≤ ∑_i H(X_i) - H(X)` for every dependence forest.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the Chow–Liu divergence

nodes.summary: The divergence `D(P ‖ P_τ) = ∑_x P(x) log₂ (P(x) / P_τ(x))` of `P` from Chow–Liu's approximation, in bits (`divergence_eq_klDiv`).
nodes.title: Divergence from the Chow–Liu approximation

nodes.summary: The approximation is a probability law: `∑_x P_τ(x) = 1`.
nodes.title: Chow–Liu approximation sums to one

nodes.summary: The mutual-information weight `∑_i I(X_i; X_{j(i)})` of a dependence forest, in bits.
nodes.title: Mutual-information weight of a dependence forest

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
